what_it_is: A marketing or advertising tech stack built from many separately bought tools that were bolted together over time and do not work as one system.
why_this_week: MMA's Decoding AI for Marketing podcast (Greg Stuart, Rex Briggs) published 'Can AI Finally Fix Advertising's Frankenstack?' with Fluency CEO Mike Lane on 8 Sep 2026; the show notes warn that layering new AI tools onto fragmented platforms creates a Frankenstack.
origin: Blend of Frankenstein and tech stack. Earliest verifiable use: CIO.com interview with Scott Brinker, 18 May 2015, where he already calls it a 'humorous label'. No single coiner found.
brand_example: Podcast episode, 8 Sep 2026, guest Mike Lane (CEO, Fluency). Also Infillion, Advertising Week 2025 recap, 9 Oct 2025.
recency_evidence: Podcast episode dated 8 Sep 2026 (20 days before run, inside the 3-week podcast window). Adweek webinar 'From Frankenstack to Flow' seen only in a search snippet (27 Aug 2026), page 404, not used.
relevance: Most Türkiye/MEA brand and agency teams run stacks assembled from global and local vendors; the term names the integration problem they face before adding AI agents.
notes: No transcript available, so no direct Mike Lane quote; attribution uses the show-notes wording. Picked: Greg Stuart podcast source, clear origin, direct relevance.

what_it_is: Gen Z and gaming slang for building effortless charisma on camera, now used by brands as a social video hook.
why_this_week: Trade coverage of the marketing angle: Storyboard18 (13 Sep 2026), News4Jax (2 Sep 2026).
origin: Slang from gaming/anime communities ('farming' aura points); went global with Rayyan Arkan Dikha's Pacu Jalur boat video in mid-2025 (BBC, 11 Jul 2025).
brand_example: Hyundai Motor Asia Pacific cast Dhika as face of Hyundai Cup 2026, 'Driving ASEAN as One' (Campaign Brief Asia, 7 Aug 2026).
relevance: Useful for Gen Z social video briefs in Türkiye/MEA.
notes: Runner-up. Strong and catchy but a youth-culture meme more than a marketing concept; no Greg Stuart podcast link; underlying meme is over a year old. Good candidate for a later week.

what_it_is: Shorthand for accepting AI-made creative at 'good enough' quality because speed and volume outrank polish.
why_this_week: Digiday, 25 Sep 2026, from its AI Marketing Strategies event.
origin: Anonymous premium-beauty marketer quoted by Digiday.
relevance: Names a quality-gate tension for teams using AI production.
notes: Rejected: no named brand example; close to Workslop already in the dictionary.
